summary: Build AI strategy, digital leadership, governance, risk, and portfolio skills in five practical days. Review the course and plan your training.
lede: AI governance training connects AI initiatives with strategic priorities, investment value and accountable oversight. For professionals shaping strategy, digital transformation, governance and risk, it covers prioritizing use cases, assessing portfolio value, assigning decision rights and evaluating lifecycle risks. Participants practice creating a portfolio scorecard and governance controls, then reporting measurable outcomes through a dashboard.
audienceIntro: This AI-driven strategic management course is designed for professionals who shape AI investment, digital leadership, governance, risk, and operating-model decisions. It is especially relevant when you must connect technical proposals to strategic outcomes and explain those choices to senior decision-makers.
modules: AI Strategy Measurement with Balanced Scorecard
AI Portfolio Prioritization and Value Cases
AI Operating Models and Digital Leadership
AI Risk with NIST AI RMF
Data Governance and COBIT Decision Rights
prerequisites: Participant level: Intermediate. Required background: Working exposure to strategy, digital transformation, risk, data governance, technology delivery, or portfolio oversight. Coding requirement: None. The exercises use supplied Microsoft Excel templates, Microsoft Power BI files, governance checklists, and case datasets rather than programming environments. Preparation: You may bring a sanitized AI initiative, policy, risk concern, or investment proposal for use during the AI-driven strategic management workshops. Advanced content depth: AI engineering remains at conceptual awareness level. Portfolio management, governance mapping, risk assessment, dashboard interpretation, and roadmap development receive operational application and guided hands-on practice.
